title: Initiative dashboard for reliability health and burn alerts
creator: Marisol Gomez
description:
Summary:
Build a single-pane initiative dashboard that surfaces service-level SLI targets, current SLO attainment, granular error-budget burn rates, and automated alerting thresholds for product & platform teams. This dashboard will be the canonical place for tracking reliability initiatives, understanding which services are consuming error budget, and kickstarting rollback/canary processes when burn exceeds thresholds.

Motivation:
- Reduce time-to-detect SLO regressions across hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Provide PMs and on-call engineers with a prioritized list of services at risk and suggested mitigation steps.
- Tie error-budget consumption to initiative health and roadmap decisions (pause rollouts, escalate to infra).

Goals / Success metrics:
- Dashboard shows per-SLO burn and on a single screen for 90% of tracked services within 1 week of rollout.
- Alert noise: <2 false positives per week per team after tuning.
- Mean time to action (MTA) for high-burn alerts reduced by 35% vs baseline.
- Teams adopt the dashboard as source-of-truth for at least 3 major rollouts in Q2.

Scope (MVP):
- Per-service cards: current SLI value, SLO target, 7d burn rate, 30d burn trend.
- Team and product filters, and exportable CSV for exec reporting.
- Configurable alert thresholds (soft/hard) that map to existing PagerDuty escalation policies.
- Links from cards to: runbooks, recent deployments, and last failing traces.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Automated rollback orchestration (follow-up initiative).
- Deep root-cause analysis UI (we will link to tracing dashboards).

Acceptance criteria:
- UX: PM/ENG can filter by team and SLO in under 3 clicks and view current burn rates.
- Data: Burn calculations match the SLI backend for 95% of samples over 14 days.
- Alerts: Teams can configure at least two threshold tiers (warning/critical) and see a sample alert test.
- Docs: Confluence spec and runbook templates exist and are linked from the dashboard.

Implementation approach:
- Frontend: Console extensions with a new "Reliability" route. Design will provide high-fidelity mocks.
- Backend: Query SLI ledger and ledger-derived burn-rate API aggregated by service + time window. Add caching layer for heavy queries.
- Alerting: Reuse existing alert rules service; add translation layer from SLO thresholds to alert rule templates.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Marisol Gomez (owner), Eng leads: Aisha Rahman, Vikram Sethi, Design: Martina Liu, On-call lead: Jordan Clarke.

Risks & mitigations:
- Data lag causing stale burn numbers -> mitigation: expose data freshness timestamp and iterate caching TTLs.
- Alert fatigue -> start with conservative thresholds and a 2-week quiet period for tuning.
- Cross-team ownership confusion -> provide default mappings from services to owning teams and require confirmation during rollout.

Deliverables:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Reliability/Initiative+Dashboard+Spec
- Design mocks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-dashboard-mocks
- Backend PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3217 (stub created)
